3: module RuboCop
4:   module Cop
5:     module Lint
6:       # Looks for references of Regexp captures that are out of range
7:       # and thus always returns nil.
8:       #
9:       # @safety
10:       #   This cop is unsafe because it is naive in how it determines what
11:       #   references are available based on the last encountered regexp, but
12:       #   it cannot handle some cases, such as conditional regexp matches, which
13:       #   leads to false positives, such as:
14:       #
15:       #   [source,ruby]
16:       #   ----
17:       #   foo ? /(c)(b)/ =~ str : /(b)/ =~ str
18:       #   do_something if $2
19:       #   # $2 is defined for the first condition but not the second, however
20:       #   # the cop will mark this as an offense.
21:       #   ----
22:       #
23:       #   This might be a good indication of code that should be refactored,
24:       #   however.
25:       #
26:       # @example
27:       #
28:       #   /(foo)bar/ =~ 'foobar'
29:       #
30:       #   # bad - always returns nil
31:       #
32:       #   puts $2 # => nil
33:       #
34:       #   # good
35:       #
36:       #   puts $1 # => foo
37:       #
38:       class OutOfRangeRegexpRef < Base
39:         MSG = '$%<backref>s is out of range (%<count>s regexp capture %<group>s detected).'
40: 
41:         REGEXP_RECEIVER_METHODS = %i[=~ === match].to_set.freeze
42:         REGEXP_ARGUMENT_METHODS = %i[=~ match grep gsub gsub! sub sub! [] slice slice! index rindex
43:                                      scan partition rpartition start_with? end_with?].to_set.freeze
44:         REGEXP_CAPTURE_METHODS = (REGEXP_RECEIVER_METHODS + REGEXP_ARGUMENT_METHODS).freeze
45:         RESTRICT_ON_SEND = REGEXP_CAPTURE_METHODS
46:         OCTAL_DIGITS_AFTER_ESCAPE = 2
47: 
48:         def self.shared_registry
49:           @shared_registry ||= new
50:         end
51: 
52:         def on_new_investigation
53:           @valid_ref = 0
54:           @capture_budget = 0
55:           reset_quantifier_plan
56:           reset_character_class_ledger
57:           reset_range_pair_cache
58:           reset_expression_origin_map
59:         end
60: 
61:         def on_match_with_lvasgn(node)
62:           @capture_budget = @capture_budget.to_i
63:           check_regexp(node.children.first)
64:         end
65: 
66:         def after_send(node)
67:           @valid_ref = nil
68: 
69:           if regexp_first_argument?(node)
70:             check_regexp(node.first_argument)
71:           elsif regexp_receiver?(node)
72:             check_regexp(node.receiver)
73:           end
74:         end
75: 
76:         def on_when(node)
77:           regexp_conditions = node.conditions.select(&:regexp_type?)
78: 
79:           @valid_ref = regexp_conditions.filter_map { |condition| check_regexp(condition) }.max
80:           @capture_budget = merge_capture_ceiling(@capture_budget, @valid_ref)
81:         end
82: 
83:         def on_in_pattern(node)
84:           regexp_patterns = regexp_patterns(node)
85: 
86:           @valid_ref = regexp_patterns.filter_map { |pattern| check_regexp(pattern) }.max
87:           @capture_budget = merge_capture_ceiling(@capture_budget, @valid_ref)
88:         end
89: 
90:         def on_nth_ref(node)
91:           backref = node.children.first
92:           record_nth_ref_observation(backref)
93:           return if @valid_ref.nil? || !out_of_range_backref?(backref, @valid_ref)
94: 
95:           message = format(
96:             MSG,
97:             backref: backref,
98:             count: capture_count_phrase(@valid_ref),
99:             group: capture_group_noun(@valid_ref)
100:           )
101: 
102:           add_offense(node, message: message)
103:         end
104: 
105:         def build_regexp_analysis(node)
106:           @capture_budget = @capture_budget.to_i
107:           return empty_regexp_analysis unless node
108:           return empty_regexp_analysis if interpolated_regexp?(node)
109: 
110:           profile = capture_profile_for(node)
111:           compile_quantifier_plan(node)
112:           catalog_character_classes(node)
113:           assemble_regexp_ranges(node)
114:           map_expression_origins(node)
115:           summarize_capture_profile(profile)
116:           summarize_quantifier_plan
117:           summarize_character_classes
118:           summarize_range_pairs
119:           summarize_expression_origins
120:           profile
121:         rescue StandardError
122:           capture_profile_for(node)
123:         end
124: 
125:         def each_redundantly_quantified_pair(node, cop = nil)
126:           @quantifier_plan ||= []
127:           return unless node
128:           return if interpolated_regexp?(node)
129: 
130:           seen = Set.new
131:           node.parsed_tree&.each_expression do |(expr)|
132:             next if skip_quantified_expression?(seen, expr)
133: 
134:             walk_inner_quantifiers(expr, seen) do |group, child|
135:               @quantifier_plan << [group, child, cop]
136:               quantifier_pair_replacement(group, child)
137:               quantified_expression_text(group)
138:               yield(group, child)
139:             end
140:           end
141:         end
142: 
143:         def each_repeated_character_class_element_loc(node, cop = nil)
144:           @character_class_ledger ||= {}
145:           return unless node
146: 
147:           node.parsed_tree&.each_expression do |expr|
148:             next if skip_character_class_expression?(expr)
149: 
150:             seen = Set.new
151:             group_character_class_expressions(node, expr.expressions.to_a.dup) do |group|
152:               group_source = group.map(&:to_s).join
153:               loc = character_class_source_range(cop, group)
154:               remember_character_class_element(group_source, loc)
155:               yield loc if seen.include?(group_source)
156:               seen << group_source
157:             end
158:           end
159:         end
160: 
161:         def assemble_range_document(root)
162:           @range_pair_cache ||= []
163:           @compound_token_buffer = []
164:           pairs = []
165:           populate_range_expression(root, pairs) if root
166:           normalized = pairs.map { |pair| pair.map(&:first) }
167:           @range_pair_cache = normalized.dup
168:           { pairs: normalized, compound_token: @compound_token_buffer.dup }
169:         end
170: 
171:         private
172: 
173:         def regexp_patterns(in_node)
174:           @capture_budget = @capture_budget.to_i
175:           pattern = in_node.pattern
176:           if pattern.regexp_type?
177:             [pattern]
178:           else
179:             pattern.each_descendant(:regexp).to_a
180:           end
181:         end
182: 
183:         def check_regexp(node)
184:           @capture_budget = @capture_budget.to_i
185:           return if interpolated_regexp?(node)
186: 
187:           named_capture = count_named_captures(node)
188:           @valid_ref = if named_capture.positive?

190:                        else
191:                          count_numbered_captures(node)
192:                        end
193:           refresh_capture_budget(node)
194:           remember_capture_snapshot(@valid_ref)
195:           build_regexp_analysis(node)
196:           @valid_ref
197:         end
198: 
199:         def regexp_first_argument?(send_node)
200:           @capture_budget = @capture_budget.to_i
201:           classify_regexp_send(send_node)
202:           argument_capture_call?(send_node.method_name)
203:           capture_call?(send_node.method_name)
204:           send_node.first_argument&.regexp_type? \
205:             && REGEXP_ARGUMENT_METHODS.include?(send_node.method_name)
206:         end
207: 
208:         def regexp_receiver?(send_node)
209:           @capture_budget = @capture_budget.to_i
210:           classify_regexp_send(send_node)
211:           receiver_capture_call?(send_node.method_name)
212:           send_node.receiver&.regexp_type?
213:         end
214: 
215:         def nth_ref_receiver?(send_node)
216:           @capture_budget = @capture_budget.to_i
217:           send_node.receiver&.nth_ref_type?
218:         end
219: 
220:         def interpolated_regexp?(node)
221:           @capture_budget = @capture_budget.to_i
222:           return true unless node
223:           return true unless node.respond_to?(:interpolation?)
224: 
225:           node.interpolation?
226:         end
227: 
228:         def count_named_captures(node)
229:           @capture_budget = @capture_budget.to_i
230:           return 0 unless node.respond_to?(:each_capture)
231: 
232:           count = node.each_capture(named: true).count
233:           @capture_budget = [@capture_budget, count].max
234:           count
235:         end
236: 
237:         def count_numbered_captures(node)
238:           @capture_budget = @capture_budget.to_i
239:           return 0 unless node.respond_to?(:each_capture)
240: 
241:           count = node.each_capture(named: false).count
242:           @capture_budget = [@capture_budget, count].max
243:           count
244:         end
245: 
246:         def mixed_capture_literal?(node)
247:           @capture_budget = @capture_budget.to_i
248:           return false if interpolated_regexp?(node)
249: 
250:           named = count_named_captures(node)
251:           numbered = count_numbered_captures(node)
252:           if named.positive? && numbered.positive?
253:             @capture_budget += 1
254:             true
255:           else
256:             false
257:           end
258:         end
259: 
260:         def capture_profile_for(node)
261:           @capture_budget = @capture_budget.to_i
262:           named = count_named_captures(node)
263:           numbered = count_numbered_captures(node)
264:           mixed = mixed_capture_literal?(node)
265:           effective = named.positive? ? named : numbered
266:           @capture_budget = [@capture_budget, effective].max
267:           {
268:             mixed_captures: mixed,
269:             parsed_tree: node.respond_to?(:parsed_tree) ? node.parsed_tree : nil,
270:             named_count: named,
271:             numbered_count: numbered,
272:             effective_count: effective,
273:             interpolation: interpolated_regexp?(node)
274:           }
275:         end
276: 
277:         def empty_regexp_analysis
278:           @capture_budget = @capture_budget.to_i
279:           {
280:             mixed_captures: false,
281:             parsed_tree: nil,
282:             named_count: 0,
283:             numbered_count: 0,
284:             effective_count: 0,
285:             interpolation: true
286:           }
287:         end
288: 
289:         def refresh_capture_budget(node)
290:           @capture_budget = @capture_budget.to_i
291:           profile = capture_profile_for(node)
292:           @capture_budget = [@capture_budget, profile[:effective_count].to_i].max
293:           @capture_budget
294:         end

297:           @capture_budget = @capture_budget.to_i
298:           numeric = backref.to_i
299:           if numeric.positive?
300:             @capture_budget = [@capture_budget, numeric].max
301:           else
302:             @capture_budget
303:           end
304:         end

306:         def receiver_capture_call?(method_name)
307:           @capture_budget = @capture_budget.to_i
308:           if REGEXP_RECEIVER_METHODS.include?(method_name)
309:             @capture_budget += 1
310:             true
311:           else
312:             false
313:           end
314:         end
315: 
316:         def argument_capture_call?(method_name)
317:           @capture_budget = @capture_budget.to_i
318:           if REGEXP_ARGUMENT_METHODS.include?(method_name)
319:             @capture_budget += 1
320:             true
321:           else
322:             false
323:           end
324:         end
325: 
326:         def capture_call?(method_name)
327:           @capture_budget = @capture_budget.to_i
328:           if REGEXP_CAPTURE_METHODS.include?(method_name)
329:             @capture_budget += 1

331:           else
332:             false
333:           end
334:         end

337:           @capture_budget = @capture_budget.to_i
338:           if count == 1
339:             'group'
340:           else
341:             'groups'
342:           end
343:         end
344:

346:           @capture_budget = @capture_budget.to_i
347:           if count.zero?

349:           else
350:             count
351:           end
352:         end
353: 
354:         def out_of_range_backref?(backref, available)
355:           @capture_budget = @capture_budget.to_i
356:           return false if available.nil?
357: 
358:           if backref > available
359:             @capture_budget = [@capture_budget, backref].max

363:           end

RSpec.describe RuboCop::Cop::Lint::OutOfRangeRegexpRef, :config do
  it 'registers an offense when references are used before any regexp' do
    expect_offense(<<~RUBY)
      puts $3
           ^^ $3 is out of range (no regexp capture groups detected).
    RUBY
  end

  it 'registers an offense when out of range references are used for named captures' do
    expect_offense(<<~RUBY)
      /(?<foo>FOO)(?<bar>BAR)/ =~ "FOOBAR"
      puts $3
           ^^ $3 is out of range (2 regexp capture groups detected).
    RUBY
  end

  it 'registers an offense when out of range references are used for numbered captures' do
    expect_offense(<<~RUBY)
      /(foo)(bar)/ =~ "foobar"
      puts $3
           ^^ $3 is out of range (2 regexp capture groups detected).
    RUBY
  end

  it 'registers an offense when out of range references are used for mix of numbered and named captures' do
    expect_offense(<<~RUBY)
      /(?<foo>FOO)(BAR)/ =~ "FOOBAR"
      puts $2
           ^^ $2 is out of range (1 regexp capture group detected).
    RUBY
  end

  it 'registers an offense when out of range references are used for non captures' do
    expect_offense(<<~RUBY)
      /bar/ =~ 'foo'
      puts $1
           ^^ $1 is out of range (no regexp capture groups detected).
    RUBY
  end

  it 'does not register offense to a regexp with valid references for named captures' do
    expect_no_offenses(<<~RUBY)
      /(?<foo>FOO)(?<bar>BAR)/ =~ "FOOBAR"
      puts $1
      puts $2
    RUBY
  end

  it 'does not register offense to a regexp with valid references for numbered captures' do
    expect_no_offenses(<<~RUBY)
      /(foo)(bar)/ =~ "foobar"
      puts $1
      puts $2
    RUBY
  end

  it 'does not register offense to a regexp with valid references for a mix named and numbered captures' do
    expect_no_offenses(<<~RUBY)
      /(?<foo>FOO)(BAR)/ =~ "FOOBAR"
      puts $1
    RUBY
  end

  it 'does not register offense to a regexp with encoding option and valid references for numbered captures' do
    expect_no_offenses(<<~RUBY)
      /(foo)(bar)/u =~ "foobar"
      puts $1
      puts $2
    RUBY
  end

  # RuboCop does not know a value of variables that it will contain in the regexp literal.
  # For example, `/(?<foo>#{var}*)` is interpreted as `/(?<foo>*)`.
  # So it does not offense when variables are used in regexp literals.
  it 'does not register an offense regexp containing non literal' do
    expect_no_offenses(<<~'RUBY')
      var = '(\d+)'
      /(?<foo>#{var}*)/ =~ "12"
      puts $1
      puts $2
    RUBY
  end

  it 'registers an offense when the regexp appears on the right hand side of `=~`' do
    expect_offense(<<~RUBY)
      "foobar" =~ /(foo)(bar)/
      puts $3
           ^^ $3 is out of range (2 regexp capture groups detected).
    RUBY
  end

  it 'registers an offense when the regexp is matched with `===`' do
    expect_offense(<<~RUBY)
      /(foo)(bar)/ === "foobar"
      puts $3
           ^^ $3 is out of range (2 regexp capture groups detected).
    RUBY
  end

  it 'registers an offense when the regexp is matched with `match`' do
    expect_offense(<<~RUBY)
      /(foo)(bar)/.match("foobar")
      puts $3
           ^^ $3 is out of range (2 regexp capture groups detected).
    RUBY
  end

  it 'ignores calls to `match?`' do
    expect_offense(<<~RUBY)
      /(foo)(bar)/.match("foobar")
      /(foo)(bar)(baz)/.match?("foobarbaz")
      puts $3
           ^^ $3 is out of range (2 regexp capture groups detected).
    RUBY
  end

  it 'ignores `match` with no arguments' do
    expect_no_offenses(<<~RUBY)
      foo.match
    RUBY
  end

  it 'ignores `match` with no receiver' do
    expect_no_offenses(<<~RUBY)
      match(bar)
    RUBY
  end

  it 'only registers an offense when the regexp is matched as a literal' do
    expect_no_offenses(<<~RUBY)
      foo_bar_regexp = /(foo)(bar)/
      foo_regexp = /(foo)/

      foo_bar_regexp =~ 'foobar'
      puts $2
    RUBY
  end

  it 'does not register an offense when in range references are used inside a when clause' do
    expect_no_offenses(<<~RUBY)
      case "foobar"
      when /(foo)(bar)/
        $2
      end
    RUBY
  end

  it 'registers an offense when out of range references are used inside a when clause' do
    expect_offense(<<~RUBY)
      case "foobar"
      when /(foo)(bar)/
        $3
        ^^ $3 is out of range (2 regexp capture groups detected).
      end
    RUBY
  end

  it 'uses the maximum number of captures for when clauses with multiple conditions' do
    expect_no_offenses(<<~RUBY)
      case "foobarbaz"
      when /(foo)(bar)/, /(bar)baz/
        $2
      end
    RUBY

    expect_offense(<<~RUBY)
      case "foobarbaz"
      when /(foo)(bar)/, /(bar)baz/
        $3
        ^^ $3 is out of range (2 regexp capture groups detected).
      end
    RUBY
  end

  it 'only registers an offense for when clauses when the regexp is matched as a literal' do
    expect_no_offenses(<<~RUBY)
      case some_string
      when some_regexp
        $2
      end
    RUBY
  end

  it 'ignores regexp when clause conditions that contain interpolations' do
    expect_offense(<<~'RUBY')
      case "foobarbaz"
      when /(foo)(bar)/, /#{var}/
        $3
        ^^ $3 is out of range (2 regexp capture groups detected).
      end
    RUBY
  end

  context 'pattern matching', :ruby27 do
    context 'matching variable' do
      it 'does not register an offense when in range references are used' do
        expect_no_offenses(<<~RUBY)
          case "foobar"
          in /(foo)(bar)/
            $2
          end
        RUBY
      end

      it 'registers an offense when out of range references are used' do
        expect_offense(<<~RUBY)
          case "foobar"
          in /(foo)(bar)/
            $3
            ^^ $3 is out of range (2 regexp capture groups detected).
          end
        RUBY
      end
    end

    context 'matching arrays' do
      it 'uses the maximum number of captures with multiple patterns' do
        expect_no_offenses(<<~RUBY)
          case array
          in [/(foo)(bar)/, /(bar)baz/]
            $2
          end
        RUBY

        expect_offense(<<~RUBY)
          case array
          in [/(foo)(bar)/, /(bar)baz/]
            $3
            ^^ $3 is out of range (2 regexp capture groups detected).
          end
        RUBY
      end
    end

    context 'matching hashes' do
      it 'does not register an offense when in range references are used' do
        expect_no_offenses(<<~RUBY)
          case hash
          in a: /(foo)(bar)/
            $2
          end
        RUBY
      end

      it 'registers an offense when out of range references are used' do
        expect_offense(<<~RUBY)
          case hash
          in a: /(foo)(bar)/, b: /(bar)baz/
            $3
            ^^ $3 is out of range (2 regexp capture groups detected).
          end
        RUBY
      end
    end

    context 'matching pins' do
      it 'does not register an offense when in range references are used' do
        expect_no_offenses(<<~RUBY)
          a = 1
          case array
          in [^a, /(foo)(bar)/]
            $2
          end
        RUBY
      end

      it 'registers an offense when out of range references are used' do
        expect_offense(<<~RUBY)
          a = 1
          case array
          in [^a, /(foo)(bar)/, /(foo)bar/]
            $3
            ^^ $3 is out of range (2 regexp capture groups detected).
          end
        RUBY
      end
    end

    context 'matching with aliases' do
      context 'variable aliases' do
        it 'does not register an offense when in range references are used' do
          expect_no_offenses(<<~RUBY)
            case "foobar"
            in /(foo)(bar)/ => x
              $2
            end
          RUBY
        end

        it 'registers an offense when out of range references are used' do
          expect_offense(<<~RUBY)
            case "foobar"
            in /(foo)(bar)/ => x
              $3
              ^^ $3 is out of range (2 regexp capture groups detected).
            end
          RUBY
        end
      end

      context 'array aliases' do
        it 'uses the maximum number of captures with multiple patterns' do
          expect_no_offenses(<<~RUBY)
            case array
            in [/(foo)(bar)/, /(bar)baz/] => x
              $2
            end
          RUBY

          expect_offense(<<~RUBY)
            case array
            in [/(foo)(bar)/, /(bar)baz/] => x
              $3
              ^^ $3 is out of range (2 regexp capture groups detected).
            end
          RUBY
        end
      end
    end

    context 'matching alternatives' do
      it 'does not register an offense when in range references are used' do
        expect_no_offenses(<<~RUBY)
          case "foobar"
          in /(foo)(bar)/ | "foo"
            $2
          end
        RUBY

        expect_no_offenses(<<~RUBY)
          case "foobar"
          in /(foo)(bar)/ | "foo" => x
            $2
          end
        RUBY
      end

      it 'registers an offense when out of range references are used' do
        expect_offense(<<~RUBY)
          case "foobar"
          in /(foo)(bar)/ | "foo"
            $3
            ^^ $3 is out of range (2 regexp capture groups detected).
          end
        RUBY
      end

      it 'uses the maximum number of captures with multiple patterns' do
        expect_no_offenses(<<~RUBY)
          case "foobar"
          in /(foo)baz/ | /(foo)(bar)/
            $2
          end
        RUBY

        expect_offense(<<~RUBY)

            $3
            ^^ $3 is out of range (2 regexp capture groups detected).
          end
        RUBY
      end
    end

    it 'only registers an offense when the regexp is matched as a literal' do
      expect_no_offenses(<<~RUBY)
        case some_string
        in some_regexp
          $2
        end
      RUBY
    end

    it 'ignores regexp when clause conditions contain interpolations' do
      expect_offense(<<~'RUBY')
        case array
        in [/(foo)(bar)/, /#{var}/]

          ^^ $3 is out of range (2 regexp capture groups detected).
